original_test_intent: Drive GPUDirect RDMA traffic through the designated ConnectX-8 single-port 800G InfiniBand XDR path with NVQual Test #38 and prove the required bandwidth, latency and data integrity while the link and fabric remain correctly negotiated and free of unacceptable congestion or faults.
original_method: Bind GPU UUID/BDF, ConnectX-8 serial/port/BDF, HCA GUID, peer/switch ports and PCIe/NUMA/IOMMU path; verify 1x800G IB XDR active width/rate and GPUDirect memory registration; pin direction, message-size matrix, queue pairs, streams, concurrency, duration and thresholds; isolate the fabric; preserve baselines; collect raw payload integrity, rate, latency, retries/congestion and GPU/NIC/PCIe/fabric telemetry; stop on first data, link or fabric fault without forced reset or retry.
manual_activity: Owner/network engineer provides the licensed profile and exact 800G IB XDR topology, drains the fabric path, approves congestion and traffic limits, and owns link/fabric recovery.
required_inputs: Licensed pinned NVQual Test #38 profile plus compatible GPU, ConnectX-8 firmware/driver and CUDA/DOCA/MOFED stack
GPU UUID/BDF, HCA serial/GUID/port/BDF, peer and switch-port identities, and PCIe/NUMA/IOMMU topology
Verified 1x800G IB XDR active mode, GDR registration path, direction/message/queue/stream/concurrency/duration matrix
Bandwidth, latency, data-integrity, retry/congestion, link/error, thermal/power limits, aborts and recovery
safety_requirements: Use a dedicated drained SUT and isolated non-production IB fabric path
Preserve port, fabric, PCIe, GPU and host error baselines before traffic
Do not force speed, reset an HCA/switch/GPU, alter fabric policy or clear evidence outside the approved recipe
Stop on data mismatch, excess retry/congestion, link flap/downshift, fabric route fault, AER/NIC/GPU error, thermal/power excursion, hang or reboot
agent_execution_scope: Verify stable endpoint/fabric identity, active 800G XDR mode, direct-memory path, profile, limits and interlocks
Run only the approved Test #38 matrix over the isolated port and peer
Collect raw per-direction performance/integrity and synchronized fabric, link, device and platform evidence
Do not accept CPU-staged traffic, infer thresholds, reset/reconfigure after fault, retry automatically or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Test #38 profile and exact 1x800G IB XDR GPU-to-HCA-to-peer/switch path
Define workload matrix and integrity/performance/congestion/error/thermal limits with aborts and recovery
Review complete evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It identifies NVQual GPU Direct traffic but not the exact Test #38 profile, IB endpoints, active XDR mode, workload or limits; a generic pass cannot prove the named 800G fabric mode.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run the pinned Test #38 profile only after verifying the stable 1x800G IB XDR path and direct registration, retaining complete per-direction traffic, integrity, congestion, fabric and platform evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NVQual Test #38, 1x800G IB XDR GPU Direct mode, all-items/no-hang/no-reboot Criteria, no bundle, and 5/30-minute allocation remain; missing traffic and acceptance values are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH SINGLE-PORT 800G IB XDR GPUDIRECT QUALIFICATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Prove active XDR mode and end-to-end GDR path before traffic, then bind each throughput, latency and integrity result to direction, message size, queue depth and synchronized port/fabric counters.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds fabric and endpoint identity, active-mode verification, reproducible traffic matrix, direct-path proof, quantitative limits and coordinated recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Aggregate output can conceal lower negotiated speed, wrong HCA/peer, CPU staging, asymmetric direction, congestion retry, corruption or a recovered link flap.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An 800G RDMA workload can saturate buffers and switch credits and disrupt neighboring fabric traffic; shared production paths are outside safe scope.

project_override_considerations: An equivalent GDR benchmark may substitute only with approved direct-memory proof, the same 1x800G XDR topology, workload matrix, integrity checks and raw fabric evidence. Ethernet, ordinary host-memory RDMA or PCIe-only bandwidth does not replace this coverage.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, approved Test #38 package/profile and owner/network authorization
GPU UUID/BDF, ConnectX-8 serial/GUID/port/BDF, peer/switch-port and PCIe/NUMA/IOMMU map
Active 1x800G IB XDR link/fabric state and GPUDirect registration proof
Raw per-direction/message/queue throughput, latency and payload-integrity results with timestamps
Port and fabric congestion/retry/error counters plus GPU/NIC/PCIe/driver/dmesg/journal/BMC/SEL/thermal/power evidence
Abort/recovery or verified clean final fabric/device state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Test #38 Procedure, Criteria and same-row reviews consistently target single-port 800G IB XDR GPU Direct traffic. Missing topology/profile/limits are supplyable inputs, not conflicting intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The named IB XDR GPUDirect objective is clear. Licensed tooling, topology and thresholds are identifiable prerequisites rather than an irreducible review blocker.

review_improvement: Makes the named 1x800G IB XDR and direct-memory path independently provable and adds fabric-wide congestion, integrity and recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: High application bandwidth alone does not demonstrate the specified transport: the HCA can negotiate a lower rate, select the wrong peer or stage data through host memory. The test therefore needs separate evidence for physical/fabric mode and direct GPU memory registration before performance is interpreted. At 800G, congestion and retry counters are part of correctness because queue credit pressure can mask loss or destabilize adjacent traffic even when average throughput looks acceptable.
